Conferences.title: Embedding-Shift Distillation: Incremental Sentence Embeddings with Periodic Re-grounding

venue.name: 20th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

Conferences.abstract: Transformer sentence encoders recompute the entire prefix whenever a token is appended, which is wasteful in streaming settings that need an embedding after every token. A recurrent encoder removes that cost, but abandons the teacher's embedding space, which a populated nearest-neighbor index cannot afford to lose. We propose embedding-shift distillation: a compact gated cell learns the change each token induces in the frozen teacher's output, and an amortized hybrid encoder applies that update at constant cost between periodic re-encodings. Re-encoding once every eight tokens, it retains 93.7 – 97.8% of the teacher's retrieval quality across five teachers while spending calls on 9% of query tokens, and 98.3% when distilled on held-out in-domain text. Under every teacher it beats holding the last re-encoding at the same cadence. That budget, shared by any policy, sets serving capacity: 8× more concurrent streams per GPU. Between calls, the learned update holds a worst-step fidelity floor no hold cadence reaches, surfacing as earlier stable decisions. The advantage is regime-dependent: a seeded re-encoding student slightly exceeds the cell on short queries, and on long queries the final embedding is set by the last re-encoding alone, so the cell's regime is where constant per-token cost binds. These results indicate that a preserved embedding space can be streamed at constant cost between calls, once the budget is sized per teacher from its copy-forward residual.
Conferences.citation: Lin, Y.-K. (2027). Embedding-Shift Distillation: Incremental Sentence Embeddings with Periodic Re-grounding. In Proceedings of the 20th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL).
